KNOWN LIVE DEFECT CONFIRMED -- registry/body tag drift on the fourth gap-shape, NOT a catalog-pattern risk (does not map to any of the 15 patterns in simulation-behavior.md; it is a static cross-file consistency defect, technical-judge-shaped, not a probabilistic response-shape risk). Traced what the agent actually produces: prompt 2 (walk-and-send-off-2.md line 30) hard-codes the audit's shape vocabulary in-fence -- '...add an observation, sharpen a rule, wire a connector, or name it as a business-rules gap.' Because Claude reads the fenced prompt text verbatim (not the surrounding body headings, which the student reads but does not paste), Claude's actual audit output will tag the fourth gap category 'business-rules gap' regardless of what the body now calls it. The exercise body's 'Match each fill to its shape and home' legend was renamed today from '**Name a business-rules gap:**' to '**Bring the material in:**' (git commit 119236f), so that literal string no longer exists anywhere in the student-facing body -- the claim immediately above the legend, 'A fill looks like one of these shapes (the audit tags each gap with one)', is now false for one of the four shapes: the audit will never emit 'Bring the material in', only 'business-rules gap'. Prompt 3 (walk-and-send-off-3.md line 23) compounds the same stale vocabulary, both in its instruction text ('propose a resolution in the shape the audit named' -- i.e. whatever prompt 2 emitted, including 'business-rules gap') and in its own routing sentence ('the ./observations/ folder in your repo for observations and business-rules gaps'). walk-and-send-off-3.md's frontmatter `produces[0].location` also still reads '(observations + business-rules gaps)' -- internal prompt-graph metadata, not student-facing, but stale for the same reason.

Behavioural consequence, traced end to end: the DESTINATION is unaffected -- prompt 3's routing table independently (and correctly, coincidentally) sends 'business-rules gap' items to `./observations/`, which is the same destination the renamed 'Bring the material in' bullet names ('Tell Claude to land what you bring in `observations/`'), so no file lands in the wrong place and no persistence step breaks. The actual harm is narrower and real: a student cross-referencing Claude's audit-report labels against the body's four-shape legend to understand what Claude found will hit a label that doesn't exist in the body (Claude says 'business-rules gap', the body says 'Bring the material in') for exactly the shape whose original bullet content changed meaning as well as name -- the old bullet ('the gap IS the finding... Claude knows what it doesn't know') was reframed today into an action the student takes (fetch the material and hand it to Claude), a genuine behavioural difference the audit prompt's vocabulary doesn't reflect at all: prompt 2 still frames this shape as a gap to *name*, not material to *bring in*. This is drift in KIND, not just label: the new body bullet describes the student physically importing external material (Notion export, PDF, pasted section) that Claude cannot fetch on its own, while the audit prompt's phrasing ('the cheapest way to close the gap today: ... name it as a business-rules gap') still frames the audit's own output as the terminal action. A student picking this gap in Phase 3 who reads only the body's new framing may expect a Claude-native resolution and be surprised that the actual fix requires them to go fetch a document -- the two files no longer describe the same student action for the same shape. This is a real, structural inconsistency that should route to the technical/prompts surface for a fix (rename in walk-and-send-off-2.md line 30 and walk-and-send-off-3.md line 23 + frontmatter, or -- given the reframed bullet is now a different action, not just a rename -- a content check on whether prompt 2's shape-c wording still matches what 'Bring the material in' now means). It is recorded here, not folded into a per-prompt catalog verdict, because none of the 15 behavioral patterns this judge scores describe cross-file vocabulary/scope drift between a prompt-registry entry and body prose; forcing it into e.g. default-acceptance or file-preservation-gap would misattribute the harm. Flagging as a standalone finding for the maintainer rather than suppressing it.
